from pathlib import Path
p=Path('/workspace/candidate_trace.json')
trace=[
  {"step":1,"file":"Tests/Fuzzers/FuzzTarget.cpp","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":13,"var":"data/size","code":"dumpDataToPcapFile(data, size, tmpFile.c_str())","note":"The raw fuzz input is first serialized into a pcap/pcapng file, so the attacker controls the packet bytes that the reader will later parse."},
  {"step":2,"file":"Tests/Fuzzers/FuzzTarget.cpp","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":22,"var":"reader","code":"std::unique_ptr<pcpp::IFileReaderDevice> reader(pcpp::IFileReaderDevice::getReader(tmpFile));","note":"The generated capture file is reopened through the packet reader, which feeds the raw bytes into PcapPlusPlus parsing logic."},
  {"step":3,"file":"Tests/Fuzzers/FuzzTarget.cpp","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":44,"var":"parsedPacket","code":"pcpp::Packet parsedPacket(&rawPacket);","note":"Each packet from the capture is parsed into protocol layers, making the embedded SOME/IP-SD bytes available as structured objects."},
  {"step":4,"file":"Tests/Fuzzers/ReadParsedPacket.h","function":"readParsedPacket","line":65,"var":"someipLayer","code":"auto someipLayer = dynamic_cast<pcpp::SomeIpSdLayer*>(layer);","note":"When the parsed layer is SOME/IP-SD, the fuzz target enters the code path that inspects entries and options from the attacker-controlled packet."},
  {"step":5,"file":"Tests/Fuzzers/ReadParsedPacket.h","function":"readParsedPacket","line":70,"var":"opts","code":"auto opts = someipLayer->getOptionsFromEntry(0);","note":"The target asks the layer to enumerate options referenced by entry 0, which drives parsing of the option table from attacker-controlled packet bytes."},
  {"step":6,"file":"Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp","function":"SomeIpSdLayer::getOptionsFromEntry","line":539,"var":"remainingLen","code":"const SomeIpSdLayer::OptionsVec SomeIpSdLayer::getOptionsFromEntry(uint32_t index) const","note":"This routine walks the options region using lengths and indices stored in the packet, so malformed metadata can steer parsing past the intended bounds."},
  {"step":7,"file":"Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp","function":"SomeIpSdLayer::getOptionsFromEntry","line":551,"var":"hdrOption","code":"SomeIpSdOption::someipsdhdroptionsbase *hdrOption = (SomeIpSdOption::someipsdhdroptionsbase *)(m_Data + offset);","note":"Each loop iteration reinterprets packet bytes at the current offset as an option header without a prior bounds check on the full option body."},
  {"step":8,"file":"Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp","function":"SomeIpSdLayer::getOptionsFromEntry","line":556,"var":"option","code":"option = parseOption(optionType, offset);","note":"The option type from attacker-controlled bytes selects a concrete option wrapper, which then reads fields from the same raw packet region."},
  {"step":9,"file":"Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp","function":"SomeIpSdLayer::parseOption","line":752,"var":"return new SomeIpSdIPv4Option(this, offset);","code":"case SomeIpSdOption::OptionType::IPv4Endpoint: ... return new SomeIpSdIPv4Option(this, offset);","note":"For IPv4 option types, the parser constructs an IPv4 option object that will later interpret the raw bytes as a fixed-size IPv4 option structure."},
  {"step":10,"file":"Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp","function":"SomeIpSdIPv4Option::SomeIpSdIPv4Option","line":79,"var":"hdr","code":"someipsdhdroptionsipv4 *hdr = (someipsdhdroptionsipv4 *)getDataPtr();","note":"The constructor stores the packet-backed pointer as an IPv4 option header, so subsequent field access depends entirely on the attacker-supplied option length and layout."},
  {"step":11,"file":"Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp","function":"SomeIpSdIPv4Option::SomeIpSdIPv4Option","line":80,"var":"hdr->ipv4Address / hdr->portNumber / hdr->l4Protocol","code":"hdr->ipv4Address = ipAddress.toInt(); hdr->portNumber = htobe16(port); hdr->l4Protocol = l4Protocol;","note":"The concrete option wrapper assumes the packet contains a full IPv4 option payload; if the crafted option is shorter than expected, later reads/writes through this wrapper can run past the heap buffer and trigger the ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE sink."}
]
p.write_text(__import__('json').dumps(trace, indent=2)+'\n')
